The changes affect family-sponsored and employment-based applicants, as well as people considering the EB-5 immigrant investor program. The federal government's 2027 fiscal year begins October 1. Each fiscal year, immigrant visa limits reset, allowing the State Department and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to resume issuing visas in categories that had reached their annual limits. The fresh supply has allowed dates to advance in several family-sponsored and employment-based categories, although some employment-based categories moved backward to keep visa issuances within quarterly and annual limits. The reset is particularly significant for some Indian applicants. India's EB-2 category, which had been unavailable in September after reaching its annual limit, reopened with a Final Action Date of November 1, 2013. The unreserved EB-5 category for India also reopened, with a Final Action Date of December 1, 2023.
